formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene copolymer ('amorphous PEO'), -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600; randomly spaced oxymethylene units inserted into linear PEO chain
formulations.Notes: Li:O = 1:64. Comonomer % = EO units per (EO+CH2O) approx 9/10 based on n~9. Conductivity only shown in Fig. 4 (Arrhenius, 20-50 C) and Fig. 5 (log sigma vs Li:O); no printed values, and digitised readings of Figs. 4 and 5 disagree with each other (e.g. at 25 C ~10^-5.4 vs ~10^-6.25 S/cm), so conductivity fields left null. m~600, n~9 implies Mn roughly 250 kDa (estimated, not stated). Sample dried under vacuum at 80 C for 24 h after evaporation of acetonitrile under dry argon.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Amorphous oxyethylene-oxymethylene copolymer ('amorphous PEO'), -[(CH2CH2O)n-CH2O-]m, n varies randomly around 9, m about 600
formulations.Notes: Li:O = 1:24; the paper says this is the conductivity maximum, with conductivity dropping at higher concentrations (attributed to higher Tg and ion pairing). Impedance spectra in Figs. 1a/b, 3 and 6 (Li electrodes show an interfacial semicircle, possibly a reaction phase). Conductivity only in Figs. 4 and 5 with no printed values; digitised readings disagree (~10^-4.25 vs ~10^-4.5 S/cm at 25 C), so fields left null. The abstract/introduction states conductivity >1e-5 S/cm at 25 C for this polymer class.
formulations.Reference: E. Linden and J.R. Owen, Conductivity measurements on amorphous PEO copolymers, Solid State Ionics 28-30 (1988) 994-1000
